title: Scholialang Skills 03: canonical materialization and cross-host release gate
problem: A good skill can still drift when copied into Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop packaging, or vendored plugin trees. The repository currently has strong 0.7.2 version-parity tests, but the two new public skills need one canonical source, deterministic host materialization, trigger/metadata validation, clean bundle evidence, and a release decision that does not silently publish or force a version number.
outcome: Doctor and Verify have one canonical repo source each and deterministic supported-host materialization. Claude Code and Codex plugin trees receive validated host outputs; Claude Desktop's .mcpb is rebuilt and tested for the corresponding MCP capabilities even where the Desktop host does not expose a native skill surface. A machine-readable release gate proves version/metadata/content/conformance parity, builds clean artifacts, records checksums and a version recommendation, and stops before tag, PyPI, GitHub release, marketplace update, or global installation.
hard_constraints: One canonical source per new skill. Generated host copies must carry provenance and be reproducible; CI must fail if a generated copy is manually edited or stale.

Host-specific wording/metadata may be rendered from explicit templates or overlays, but shared procedural semantics and bundled scripts must derive from the canonical source. Do not accept copy/paste parity by convention.
Validate skill frontmatter, triggering descriptions, Codex agents/openai.yaml, bundled executable modes, relative references, and the absence of forbidden auxiliary files.

Claude Desktop capability verification must be honest: verify the .mcpb server/tools and artifact contract, and report native_skill_surface=false if that host does not load SKILL.md. Do not pretend an MCP server bundle is a native skill installation.
Build from a clean isolated checkout/environment. Record artifact hashes, source commit, package/plugin/grammar axes, test commands, and required-scenario verdicts.

Do not choose or apply a package version bump unless repository policy makes it mechanically unambiguous. Emit a recommendation with rationale and leave version mutation for explicit release approval.
No publication, tag, GitHub release, PyPI upload, marketplace push, public announcement, global install, or default-branch write.
Run all new skill tests and the existing release-version, public-hygiene, MCP protocol/support, vendored-contract, and .mcpb tests.
success_metrics: Two independent materializations of each supported host output are byte-identical and match committed generated copies.
Claude Code and Codex skills pass metadata, trigger, resource, executable-mode, and semantic parity checks.
The clean .mcpb build passes its public MCP capability scenarios and explicitly reports whether a native skill surface exists.
A machine-readable release gate records commit, version axes, checksums, tests, required scenarios, and a non-binding version recommendation with zero publication side effects.

stories.title: Materialize canonical skills deterministically into supported hosts
stories.description: Implement canonical-to-host rendering/sync for Doctor and Verify, including explicit host overlays where needed, provenance, executable modes, and stale-copy detection. Generate Codex UI metadata from final skill content.

stories.title: Run the cross-host and clean-artifact conformance matrix
stories.description: Validate Claude Code and Codex skill surfaces and the Claude Desktop MCP bundle in isolated environments. Assert semantic parity without falsely claiming Desktop has a native skill surface.

stories.title: Produce a no-publish release gate and version recommendation
stories.description: Emit machine-readable release evidence with source commit, version axes, reproducible hashes, scenario/test outcomes, residual risks, and version recommendation. Stop before every publication or version mutation gate.
